sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是安德鲁·罗斯·索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at the
sentences.zh: 我负责《纽约时报》每日简讯 DealBook 的商业与政策报道。

sentences.en: New York Times.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市的 DealBook 峰会现场采访商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的几位领袖，其中包括 J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜

sentences.en: Lagarde, Zylran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 拉加德、齐尔兰·蒙达尼以及许多其他人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以实时观看其中一些毫无防备、未经过滤的对话。

sentences.en: We're going to be live-streaming select interviews for anyone to watch free at nytimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我们将在 nytimes.com 上直播精选采访，供任何人免费观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅者，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序进行观看，并免费获得一个月的所有新闻报道权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望大家准时收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是来自《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴尔巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这里是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Today,
sentences.zh: 今天，

sentences.en: 20 Democratic candidates have now made their case to American voters.
sentences.zh: 已有20位民主党候选人向美国选民阐述了他们的主张。

sentences.en: Alex Burns on the differing visions for the future, the breakout performances, and where it leaves the race.
sentences.zh: 亚历克斯·伯恩斯将探讨对未来的不同愿景、异军突起者的表现，以及这对选战格局的影响。

sentences.en: It's Friday, June 28th.
sentences.zh: 今天是6月28日，星期五。

sentences.en: So, Alex Burns, it's 2.25 p.m.
sentences.zh: 那么，亚历克斯·伯恩斯，现在是下午2点25分。

sentences.en: on Thursday.
sentences.zh: 星期四。

sentences.en: So we're talking in between the two sets of Democratic debates.
sentences.zh: 所以我们是在两场民主党辩论的间隙进行交谈。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: We're in this very long intermission in this sort of multi-part extravaganza.
sentences.zh: 我们正处于这场长篇大戏中非常漫长的中场休息阶段。

sentences.en: We had 10 candidates last night.
sentences.zh: 昨晚我们有10位候选人。

sentences.en: We're going to have 10 candidates tonight.
sentences.zh: 今晚我们还将有10位候选人。

sentences.en: They were sorted out more or less randomly by the Democratic National Committee.
sentences.zh: 他们是由民主党全国委员会大致随机分组的。

sentences.en: On the first night, the tone really set by the insurgent wing of the party embodied by Elizabeth Warren.
sentences.zh: 在第一晚，辩论基调实际上是由伊丽莎白·沃伦所代表的党内激进派确定的。

sentences.en: For the second night, the tone very clearly going to be set by the more establishment, moderate, incrementalist wing of the party embodied in Joe Biden.
sentences.zh: 而在第二晚，辩论基调则非常明显地由乔·拜登所代表的党内建制派、温和派和渐进派定下。

sentences.en: Good evening, everyone.
sentences.zh: 大家晚上好。

sentences.en: I'm Lester Holt, and welcome to the first Democratic debate in the 2020 race for president.
sentences.zh: 我是莱斯特·霍尔特，欢迎收看2020年总统大选的首场民主党辩论。

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Savannah Guthrie, and tonight is our first- So who was on stage on night number one, Wednesday night?
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是萨凡纳·格思里，今晚是我们的第一场——那么，周三第一晚都有谁登台了？

sentences.en: On all of them?
sentences.zh: 全部都要说吗？

sentences.en: You're going to struggle to remember all the time, are you?
sentences.zh: 你总是记不住所有名字吧？

sentences.en: I certainly am.
sentences.zh: 我当然记不住。

sentences.en: Look, the most prominent- Didn't you watch the debate?
sentences.zh: 听着，最著名的是——你没看辩论吗？

sentences.en: I did, man.
sentences.zh: 我看过了，老兄。

sentences.en: It was two hours.
sentences.zh: 整整两个小时。

sentences.en: So-
sentences.zh: 所以——

sentences.en: Well, now it's time to find out.
sentences.zh: 好吧，现在就要见分晓了。

sentences.en: Tonight, round one, New Jersey Senator Cory Booker.
sentences.zh: 今晚第一轮，新泽西州参议员科里·布克。

sentences.en: Elizabeth Warren, Cory Booker, Amy Klobuchar, big senators in this race, big figures in the party.
sentences.zh: 伊丽莎白·沃伦、科里·布克、艾米·克洛布查尔，这些都是本次竞选中的重量级参议员，党内的重要人物。

sentences.en: You have Beto O'Rourke, former Texas Senate candidate, Julian Castro, former housing secretary,
sentences.zh: 还有前德克萨斯州参议员候选人贝托·奥鲁克、前住房部长朱利安·卡斯特罗，

sentences.en: Jay Inslee, the governor of Washington state.
sentences.zh: 华盛顿州州长杰伊·英斯利。

sentences.en: Three current or former members of the House,
sentences.zh: 三位现任或前任众议员，

sentences.en: Tulsi Gabbard of Hawaii, John Delaney of Maryland, Tim Ryan of Ohio, and then Bill de Blasio, the mayor of New York.
sentences.zh: 夏威夷州的图尔西·加巴德、马里兰州的约翰·德拉尼、俄亥俄州的蒂姆·瑞恩，还有纽约市长比尔·德布拉西奥。

sentences.en: And how does this debate begin?
sentences.zh: 这场辩论是如何开始的？

sentences.en: And we'll start this evening with Senator Elizabeth Warren.
sentences.zh: 今晚我们从参议员伊丽莎白·沃伦开始。

sentences.en: Senator, good evening to you.
sentences.zh: 参议员，晚上好。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: You have many plans-
sentences.zh: 你有很多计划——

sentences.en: Well, it begins, like so much else in this race, with Elizabeth Warren setting the tone, setting the ideological stakes, setting the frame for the argument.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这场辩论的开局和这场竞选中的很多事情一样，是由伊丽莎白·沃伦定下基调、设定意识形态赌注以及确立辩论框架开始的。

sentences.en: What do you say to those who worry this kind of significant change could be risky to the economy?
sentences.zh: 你对那些担心这种重大变革可能会危及经济的人有什么看法？

sentences.en: So I think of it this way.
sentences.zh: 我是这样看的。

sentences.en: Who is this economy really working for?
sentences.zh: 这个经济体究竟是在为谁服务？

sentences.en: Right out of the gate, she is talking about big structural change in the country.
sentences.zh: 一开场，她就在谈论这个国家的重大结构性变革。

sentences.en: It's doing great for giant drug companies.
sentences.zh: 这对大型制药公司来说好得不得了。

sentences.en: It's just not doing great for people who are trying to get a prescription filled.
sentences.zh: 但对那些正努力抓药的人来说却一点也不好。

sentences.en: And denouncing basically the economic system and government as a whole is corrupt.
sentences.zh: 她基本上谴责了整个经济系统和政府都是腐败的。

sentences.en: We need to call it out.
sentences.zh: 我们必须大声指出来。

sentences.en: We need to attack it head on.
sentences.zh: 我们必须正面抨击它。

sentences.en: And we need to make structural change in our government, in our economy, and in our country.
sentences.zh: 我们必须对我们的政府、经济和国家进行结构性变革。

sentences.en: So it begins with a pretty clear, blow-it-up statement from Elizabeth Warren.
sentences.zh: 所以，辩论以伊丽莎白·沃伦一段相当明确的“全盘推翻”式发言开场。

sentences.en: It does.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And it's her ideas that then really dominate the first hour of this debate.
sentences.zh: 而且正是她的理念随后主导了这场辩论的第一个小时。

sentences.en: Senator Warren, in particular, put out a plan to break up tech companies-
sentences.zh: 沃伦参议员，特别是提出了一项拆分科技公司的计划——

sentences.en: Where you have other candidates being asked to respond to her agenda.
sentences.zh: 其他候选人被要求对她的议程做出回应。

sentences.en: I feel very strongly about the need to check the corporate consolidation and let the free market work.
sentences.zh: 我坚信有必要遏制企业垄断，让自由市场发挥作用。

sentences.en: And then Elizabeth Warren getting to respond to them, responding to her.
sentences.zh: 然后伊丽莎白·沃伦得以回应他们，对他们做出反驳。

sentences.en: Senator Warren, I mentioned you.
sentences.zh: 沃伦参议员，我提到了你。

sentences.en: If you wanted a really vivid picture of the way her plan and policy-driven campaign has really set the terms of this race for the other folks running, this was it.
sentences.zh: 如果你想真切地了解她的计划和政策驱动型竞选如何为其他参选人设定了这场竞选的条款，这就是例子。

sentences.en: I have the courage to go after them.
sentences.zh: 我有勇气对付他们。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: So once Elizabeth Warren sets the tone, what stands out to you next?
sentences.zh: 那么，一旦伊丽莎白·沃伦定下了基调，接下来什么最吸引你的注意？

sentences.en: All right, we're going to turn to the issue of health care right now.
sentences.zh: 好的，我们现在转向医疗保健议题。

sentences.en: I'd really try to understand whether there may or may not be daylight between-
sentences.zh: 我真的很想弄清楚之间究竟有没有分歧——

sentences.en: There's this really, really revealing moment on health care where the whole field is asked,
sentences.zh: 在医疗保健问题上有一个非常、非常有启示意义的时刻，全场的候选人都被问到：

sentences.en: Who here would abolish their private health insurance in favor of a government-run plan?
sentences.zh: 这里有谁会为了政府运营的计划而废除他们的私人健康保险？

sentences.en: Just a show of hands to start off with.
sentences.zh: 先举手示意一下。

sentences.en: You have two candidates who say that they're in favor of that approach.
sentences.zh: 有两位候选人表示他们赞成这种做法。

sentences.en: One of them is Warren.
sentences.zh: 其中一位是沃伦。

sentences.en: The other one is Bill de Blasio.
sentences.zh: 另一位是比尔·德布拉西奥。

sentences.en: And why is that surprising?
sentences.zh: 为什么这令人惊讶？

sentences.en: Warren has been pretty careful on the single-payer issue, that she has signed on to a Bernie Sanders Medicare-for-all bill,
sentences.zh: 沃伦在全民医保问题上一直相当谨慎，她签署了伯尼·桑德斯的“全民医保法案”，

sentences.en: but she has sort of repeatedly stopped short of going full Bernie and saying, let's get rid of private health insurance and just do Canadian-style or European-style system instead.
sentences.zh: 但她多次没有选择彻底效仿伯尼，即废除私人医疗保险，转而采用加拿大式或欧洲式的系统。

sentences.en: There are a lot of politicians who say, oh, it's just not possible, we just can't do it, have a lot of political reasons for this.
sentences.zh: 有很多政客说，哦，这根本不可能，我们做不到，并为此找了很多政治理由。

sentences.en: What they're really telling you is they just won't fight for it.
sentences.zh: 他们真正想告诉你的是，他们根本不会为此奋斗。

sentences.en: She knows who her competition is in this primary right now, that she has risen in this race.
sentences.zh: 她很清楚自己在初选中的竞争对手是谁，她在本次竞选中支持率上升了。

sentences.en: Bernie Sanders has fallen almost in direct proportion.
sentences.zh: 而伯尼·桑德斯的支持率几乎成正比地下降了。

sentences.en: His voters are moving in her direction, and presumably she wants to keep on attracting more of them.
sentences.zh: 他的选民正在向她靠拢，想必她希望继续吸引更多这样的人。

sentences.en: It could come at a price, though.
sentences.zh: 不过，这可能需要付出代价。

sentences.en: It's a much politically riskier position to take.
sentences.zh: 这是一个政治风险大得多的立场。

sentences.en: You have moderate voters she would need to win in a general election.
sentences.zh: 她在广义大选中需要赢得温和派选民的支持。

sentences.en: You have moderate voters who might be available to her in a primary who might shy away from that kind of message.
sentences.zh: 初选中也有些温和派选民可能会对这种信息敬而远之。

sentences.en: We'll see what else she says on health care in the coming weeks and months, whether she really does allow there to be no daylight at all between her and Bernie Sanders.
sentences.zh: 我们将拭目以待她在未来几周和几个月里就医疗保健发表什么言论，看她是否真的允许自己与伯尼·桑德斯之间毫无保留、完全一致。

sentences.en: But we saw pretty quickly there was significant daylight between her and a couple other people on that stage.
sentences.zh: 但我们很快就看到，她与舞台上的其他几个人之间存在着明显的分歧。

sentences.en: Well, I think it's a bold approach.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为这是一个大胆的方法。

sentences.en: It's something that Barack Obama wanted to do when we were working on the Affordable Care Act.
sentences.zh: 这是我们在制定《平价医疗法案》时巴拉克·奥巴马想要做的事情。

sentences.en: And that is a...
sentences.zh: 那是一个……

sentences.en: The most interesting response to me was Amy Klobuchar, the senator from Minnesota.
sentences.zh: 对我来说最有趣的回应来自明尼苏达州参议员艾米·克洛布查尔。

sentences.en: She has run as a pretty explicitly moderate candidate in this race.
sentences.zh: 她在这场竞选中一直以非常明确的温和派候选人身份参选。

sentences.en: And she didn't just talk about an alternative idea, but she talked about what she sees as essentially the political folly of the idea that Warren endorsed.
sentences.zh: 她不仅谈到了一种替代方案，还谈到了她所认为的沃伦所认可的那种方案本质上的政治愚蠢之处。

sentences.en: I am just simply concerned about kicking half of America off of their health insurance in four years, which is exactly what this bill says.
sentences.zh: 我只是单纯担心在四年内把半数美国人踢出他们的医疗保险，而这正是该法案所说的。

sentences.en: Which is what that Bernie Sanders bill does.
sentences.zh: 也就是伯尼·桑德斯法案所做的事情。

sentences.en: Let me turn to Senator Booker on this.
sentences.zh: 让我把话题转向布克参议员。

sentences.en: Senator Booker, explain to me where you are.
sentences.zh: 布克参议员，请向我解释一下你的立场。

sentences.en: The other person who I thought was interesting on health care was Cory Booker.
sentences.zh: 我觉得在医疗保健问题上另一个很有意思的人是科里·布克。

sentences.en: I absolutely will.
sentences.zh: 我当然会。

sentences.en: First of all, we're talking about this as a health care issue, but in communities like mine, low-income communities like mine, it's an education issue.
sentences.zh: 首先，我们把这当作一个医疗保健问题来讨论，但在像我这样的社区、像我这样的低收入社区，这是一个教育问题。

sentences.en: He was sort of a midpoint between Elizabeth Warren's let's overhaul the entire system from top to bottom and Amy Klobuchar's sort of unapologetically incrementalist alternative.
sentences.zh: 他是伊丽莎白·沃伦的“全盘推翻整个系统”与艾米·克洛布查尔的“毫不掩饰的渐进主义替代方案”之间的一个折中点。

sentences.en: And I believe the best way to get there is Medicare for all, but I have an urgency about this.
sentences.zh: 我相信实现这一目标的最佳途径是全民医保，但我对此有一种紧迫感。

sentences.en: He basically attempted to try to split the baby and say...
sentences.zh: 他基本上试图两面兼顾，并表示……

sentences.en: Wait, we have to do the things immediately that are going to provide better care.
sentences.zh: 等等，我们必须立即做那些能够提供更好护理的事情。

sentences.en: But thinks that change has to happen right now, and he's in favor of doing the things immediately that would expand coverage.
sentences.zh: 但他认为变革必须现在发生，他赞成立即采取能够扩大医疗保障范围的行动。

sentences.en: The implicit message there is single-payer is not going to happen overnight, so it's not something that he would promise to do in the first year of his administration.
sentences.zh: 这里隐含的信息是，单一支付方医疗体制不会在一夜之间实现，所以这不是他承诺在执政第一年就会做的事情。

sentences.en: It's a pattern we saw a couple times in that debate, usually with Warren and Klobuchar as the two poles of the argument and the other candidates lined up in between.
sentences.zh: 我们在那场辩论中多次看到这种模式，通常以沃伦和克洛布查尔作为辩论的两个极点，其他候选人则排列在中间。

sentences.en: Watching that image of Oscar and his daughter Valeria is heartbreaking.
sentences.zh: 看到奥斯卡和他的女儿瓦莱里亚的那张照片令人心碎。

sentences.en: It should also piss us all off.
sentences.zh: 这也应该让我们所有人感到愤怒。

sentences.en: There was a different policy issue entirely where Elizabeth Warren was not a major player
sentences.zh: 还有一个完全不同的政策议题，伊丽莎白·沃伦并不是其中的主要参与者，

sentences.en: in the conversation where you had Julian Castro and Beto O'Rourke really going at it over immigration policy.
sentences.zh: 在那个议题中，朱利安·卡斯特罗和贝托·奥鲁克就移民政策展开了激烈的交锋。

sentences.en: The reason that they're separating these little children from their families is that they're using Section 1325 of that act...
sentences.zh: 他们把这些小孩子与家人分离的原因是，他们正在利用该法案的第1325条……

sentences.en: And whether the next Democratic president ought to try to reform the system on an ambitious scale, but on a pretty conventional set of Democratic policies,
sentences.zh: 以及下一任民主党总统是否应该尝试以雄心勃勃的规模，但在一套相当传统的民主党政策下来改革该系统，

sentences.en: or whether they should do something that essentially kicks out one of the pillars of the current enforcement system entirely.
sentences.zh: 还是应该采取彻底拆除当前执法系统支柱之一的行动。

sentences.en: Some of us on this stage have called to end that section, to terminate it.
sentences.zh: 我们舞台上的一些人已经呼吁废除该条款，彻底终结它。

sentences.en: Some, like Congressman O'Rourke, have not.
sentences.zh: 有些人，比如奥鲁克众议员，则没有。

sentences.en: And I want to challenge all of the candidates to do that.
sentences.zh: 我想向所有候选人发出挑战，要求他们这样做。

sentences.en: That's Julian Castro's proposal to repeal the law that makes unlawful border crossing a criminal offense rather than just a civil offense.
sentences.zh: 这是朱利安·卡斯特罗的提议，即废除将非法越境定为刑事犯罪而非单纯民事违法的法律。

sentences.en: Essentially decriminalizing undocumented immigration.
sentences.zh: 本质上是将无证移民非罪化。

sentences.en: Literally decriminalizing.
sentences.zh: 字面上的非罪化。

sentences.en: And the Beto O'Rourke alternative...
sentences.zh: 而贝托·奥鲁克的替代方案是……

sentences.en: Actually, as a member of Congress, I helped to introduce legislation that would ensure that we don't criminalize those who are seeking asylum and refuge in this country.
sentences.zh: 实际上，作为一名国会议员，我曾协助提出立法，以确保我们不会将那些在这个国家寻求庇护和避难的人定为罪犯。

sentences.en: If you're fleeing desperation...
sentences.zh: 如果你是在逃离绝望……

sentences.en: He has put out a suite of immigration reform policies that don't really touch that Castro proposal.
sentences.zh: 他提出了一套移民改革政策，但并没有真正触及卡斯特罗的那个提议。

sentences.en: They focus on doing things like increasing the capacity of the immigration system
sentences.zh: 他们的重点是做一些事情，比如提高移民系统的处理能力，

sentences.en: to process people, not detaining people who are not accused of crimes besides immigration offenses, adding all the sorts of protections for DREAMers and other undocumented folks
sentences.zh: 以处理人员流动，不拘留除了移民违规之外没有被指控犯罪的人，并为民主党人长期倡导的“逐梦人”及其他无证人群增加各种保护。

sentences.en: that Democrats have advocated for for a long time.
sentences.zh: 民主党人长期以来一直倡导这些保护措施。

sentences.en: We would not turn back Valeria and her father, Oscar.
sentences.zh: 我们不会将瓦莱里亚和她的父亲奥斯卡拒之门外。

sentences.en: We would accept them into this country and follow our own asylum laws.
sentences.zh: 我们会接纳他们进入这个国家，并遵守我们自己的庇护法。

sentences.en: So at this point in the debate, after hearing the way these candidates are breaking down on health care and now on undocumented immigration, what are you thinking?
sentences.zh: 所以在辩论的这个阶段，在听了这些候选人在医疗保健以及现在的无证移民问题上的立场后，你在想什么？

sentences.en: I'm thinking that, among other things, this shows how the center of gravity in this party has moved very, very substantially to the left since 2016,
sentences.zh: 我在想，除其他事项外，这表明了这个政党的重心自2016年以来已经向左大幅度偏移，

sentences.en: that these ideas for single-payer health care, for decriminalizing certain kinds of border crossing, these are not seen as fringe ideas.
sentences.zh: 这些关于单一支付方医保、将某些越境行为非罪化的理念，不再被视为边缘观点。

sentences.en: They're not even seen by much of the party as terribly controversial or dangerous ideas.
sentences.zh: 党内的大多数人甚至不认为它们是极其具争议性或危险的想法。

sentences.en: These are entirely within the mainstream of democratic politics right now.
sentences.zh: 这些完全属于当前民主党政治的主流。

sentences.en: That wasn't true at this point in 2015.
sentences.zh: 在2015年的这个时候并非如此。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: No one on that stage was dismissing out of hand the idea of upending the current health care system
sentences.zh: 台上的任何人都没有不假思索地排斥颠覆现有医疗体系的想法，

sentences.en: or decriminalizing illegal border crossings, which is, I guess, a major moment for the party.
sentences.zh: 或是将非法越境非罪化的想法，我想这对该党来说是一个重大的时刻。

sentences.en: And in fact, the people who were pushing back on those ideas were doing so.
sentences.zh: 事实上，那些反击这些想法的人，他们的确这样做了。

sentences.en: And I am happy to look at his proposal, but I do think you want to make sure that...
sentences.zh: 我很乐意研究他的提案，但我确实认为你想确保……

sentences.en: Almost apologetically or certainly carefully and defensively.
sentences.zh: 几乎带有一点歉意，或者肯定是非常小心和防备的。

sentences.en: Why do you disagree?
sentences.zh: 为什么你不同意？

sentences.en: I don't think I disagree.
sentences.zh: 我不认为我不同意。

sentences.en: I think we have a serious problem in our country.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们国家面临着一个严重的问题。

sentences.en: There's a level of concern, even among moderate Democrats, folks who are proud of their center-left credentials.
sentences.zh: 人们普遍感到担忧，甚至连温和派民主党人、那些为其左翼中间派立场感到自豪的人也是如此。

sentences.en: There's a level of sensitivity to the fact that this is a party that, basically in its DNA,
sentences.zh: 大家敏感地意识到，这个政党在其基因里

sentences.en: wants to do big liberal things and has to be persuaded to go about doing them differently.
sentences.zh: 就有着做宏大自由主义议程的冲动，只是需要被说服去用不同的方式来实现。

sentences.en: I am in this fight because I believe that we can make our government, we can make our economy, we can make our country work, not just for those at the top.
sentences.zh: 我之所以参加这场竞选，是因为我相信我们可以让政府、让经济、让国家为所有人服务，而不仅仅是为了处于金字塔尖的人。

sentences.en: We can make it work for everyone.
sentences.zh: 我们可以让它为每个人服务。

sentences.en: And I promise you this, I will fight for you as hard as I fight for my own family.
sentences.zh: 我向你们保证，我会为你们奋斗，就像为我自己的家人奋斗一样拼尽全力。

sentences.en: So, from what you're saying, the blow-it-up camp has a built-in advantage in this debate, and everybody seems to be orienting themselves around them.
sentences.zh: 所以，按你所说，主张彻底推翻重来阵营在这场辩论中有着天生的优势，每个人似乎都在围绕着他们调整自己的立场。

sentences.en: I don't think there was any indication last night that someone other than Elizabeth Warren became a more dominant presence on that stage, that she set the tone at the beginning,
sentences.zh: 我认为昨晚没有任何迹象表明，除了伊丽莎白·沃伦之外，还有谁成为了那个舞台上更具统治力的存在，是她定下了开场的基调，

sentences.en: she set the tone at the end.
sentences.zh: 也是她定下了收尾的基调。

sentences.en: I'd be very surprised if you saw her poll numbers change for the worse.
sentences.zh: 如果你看到她的民调支持率没有变差，我将感到非常惊讶。

sentences.en: And that will do it for night one of this two-night event.
sentences.zh: 第一晚的辩论到这里就结束了，这是一场为期两天的活动。

sentences.en: And guess what?
sentences.zh: 你猜怎么着？

sentences.en: We've got 10 more candidates tomorrow night.
sentences.zh: 明晚我们还有10位候选人。

sentences.en: So, by the end of night one, we have a debate dominated by those calling for the most significant structural changes in our economy, in our society, in our political system.
sentences.zh: 因此，在第一晚结束时，我们看到了一场由那些呼吁对我们的经济、社会和政治体制进行最深刻结构性变革的人主导的辩论。

sentences.en: How does that set up what we're going to see on night two, Thursday night?
sentences.zh: 这为我们在周四晚上的第二晚辩论奠定了怎样的基调？

sentences.en: Look, I think if last night's debate were the only debate, that there were only those 10 candidates, or if you watched last night's debate and somehow missed tonight's debate,
sentences.zh: 听着，我认为如果昨晚的辩论是唯一的辩论，如果只有那10位候选人，或者如果你看了昨晚的辩论却阴差阳错地错过了今晚的辩论，

sentences.en: you would come away thinking that the Democratic Party was defined by this real ethos of blow it up, change the system, break up the system.
sentences.zh: 你就会觉得民主党是由这种彻底砸烂、改变体制、摧毁体制的真正精神所定义的。

sentences.en: You would not know that the leading figure in the race, by a good margin at this point, is the ultimate institutionalist, the ultimate incremental,
sentences.zh: 你不会知道，目前在竞选中以明显优势领先的人物，恰恰是体制派的化身，是渐进主义的终极代表，

sentences.en: let's just work within the system as it currently exists, make some positive changes here or there, but basically leave things intact.
sentences.zh: 主张就在现有的体制内运作，在这里或那里做出一些积极的改变，但基本上保持原状。

sentences.en: And that's Joe Biden.
sentences.zh: 那个人就是乔·拜登。

sentences.en: Well, we will check back in with you in a few hours and we'll find out if you're right.
sentences.zh: 好的，我们会在几个小时后再来找你，看看你到底说得对不对。

sentences.en: We'll see.
sentences.zh: 我们拭目以待。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的应用程序？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 免费畅读？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to the Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 众所周知，你需要订阅《时报》才能查阅所有报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore the Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但如果你能免费体验《时报》一个月，且无需输入信用卡信息呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download the New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你首次下载《纽约时报》应用程序时，你在该应用中的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 有一个月的时间去突破付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么内容。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to the New York Times, download the Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没有订阅《纽约时报》，请立即下载《时报》应用，并获得30天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: Okay, Alex, it is now 12.15 on Friday morning.
sentences.zh: 好的，亚历克斯，现在是周五凌晨12点15分。

sentences.en: Thank you for doing this again.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你再次接受采访。

sentences.en: Who was on stage this time?
sentences.zh: 这次有哪些人上了台？

sentences.en: Well, because it's 12.15 a.m., I did come prepared with notes for this question.
sentences.zh: 好吧，因为现在是凌晨12点15分，我确实为这个问题准备好了笔记。

sentences.en: We had Joe Biden and Bernie Sanders as sort of the most major candidates on stage going into the debate.
sentences.zh: 在进入辩论时，我们有乔·拜登和伯尼·桑德斯作为台面上最重要的几位候选人。

sentences.en: Kamala Harris and Pete Buttigieg.
sentences.zh: 卡玛拉·哈里斯和皮特·布蒂吉格。

sentences.en: And then the supporting cast of the debate, John Hickenlooper, the former governor of Colorado.
sentences.zh: 然后是辩论的配角阵容，科罗拉多州前州长约翰·希肯卢珀。

sentences.en: Michael Bennett, senator from Colorado.
sentences.zh: 来自科罗拉多州的联邦参议员迈克尔·贝内特。

sentences.en: Kirsten Gillibrand, our senator here in New York.
sentences.zh: 我们在纽约的参议员克尔斯滕·吉利布兰德。

sentences.en: Congressman Eric Swalwell.
sentences.zh: 国会议员埃里克·斯瓦韦尔。

sentences.en: And then Andrew Yang and Marianne Williamson, the real political newcomers in the race.
sentences.zh: 还有安德鲁·杨和玛丽安娜·威廉姆森，他们是这场竞选中真正的政治新面孔。

sentences.en: Nailed it.
sentences.zh: 说得全中。

sentences.en: Bravo.
sentences.zh: 干得漂亮。

sentences.en: And you did have a cheat sheet.
sentences.zh: 而且你确实带了小抄。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: How did the second debate begin?
sentences.zh: 第二场辩论是如何开始的？

sentences.en: We're going to start today with Senator Sanders.
sentences.zh: 我们今天将从桑德斯参议员开始。

sentences.en: Good evening to you.
sentences.zh: 晚上好。

sentences.en: So from the very start, you have this stark ideological contrast between Bernie Sanders and Joe Biden.
sentences.zh: 因此，从一开始，伯尼·桑德斯和乔·拜登之间就形成了鲜明的意识形态对比。

sentences.en: The very first question goes to Bernie Sanders.
sentences.zh: 第一个问题直接抛给了伯尼·桑德斯。

sentences.en: My question to you is, will taxes go up for the middle class in a Sanders administration?
sentences.zh: 我给你的问题是，在桑德斯政府的领导下，中产阶级的税收会上升吗？

sentences.en: And if so, how do you sell that to voters?
sentences.zh: 如果是的话，你如何向选民推销这一点？

sentences.en: Well, strikingly, but also in a very on-brand way, he essentially stuck to his guns on that.
sentences.zh: 引人注目的是，但也非常符合他一贯的风格，他在这个问题上基本上坚持了自己的立场。

sentences.en: People who have health care under Medicare for all will have no premiums, no deductibles, no copayments, no out-of-pocket expenses.
sentences.zh: 在“全民医保”计划下获得医疗保障的人将无需支付保费、免赔额、共付额，也没有自付费用。

sentences.en: Yes, they will pay more in taxes, but less in health care for what they get.
sentences.zh: 是的，他们的税会交得更多，但就他们所获得的医疗保障而言，医疗开支反而会减少。

sentences.en: Thank you, Senator.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，参议员。

sentences.en: But that in the big picture, he was entirely happy to make this very blunt populist argument that, yeah, you've got to take the insurance companies out of the picture,
sentences.zh: 但在宏观层面上，他完全乐意提出这种非常直率的民粹主义论点，即：是的，你必须把保险公司排除在外，

sentences.en: you've got to pay more to the government, and you've got to restructure the system from top to bottom.
sentences.zh: 你必须向政府缴纳更多税款，你必须从头到脚重组这个系统。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: You've got to blow it up.
sentences.zh: 你必须把它彻底砸碎。

sentences.en: We think it is time for change, real change.
sentences.zh: 我们认为现在是做出改变的时候了，真正的改变。

sentences.en: And by that, I mean that health care, in my view, is a human right.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在我看来，医疗保健是一项人权。

sentences.en: And Joe Biden is asked about the speech, Alex, that you have focused on.
sentences.zh: 亚历克斯，乔·拜登被问及了你所关注的那次演讲。

sentences.en: You said, we shouldn't, quote, demonize the rich.
sentences.zh: 你说过，我们不应该，引述原话，妖魔化富人。

sentences.en: You said, nobody has to be punished.
sentences.zh: 你说过，没有人必须受到惩罚。

sentences.en: No one's standard of living would change.
sentences.zh: 没有人的生活水平会发生变化。

sentences.en: Nothing would fundamentally—
sentences.zh: 没有什么会根本性地——

sentences.en: Essentially, nothing's really going to change in America under a Biden presidency.
sentences.zh: 本质上，在拜登执政期间，美国的现状不会发生真正的改变。

sentences.en: Obviously, a very stark difference with Bernie Sanders.
sentences.zh: 显然，这与伯尼·桑德斯形成了非常鲜明的对比。

sentences.en: And Biden sort of pivots out of it.
sentences.zh: 而拜登则试图巧妙地把话题岔开。

sentences.en: What I meant by that is, look, Donald Trump thinks Wall Street built America.
sentences.zh: 我这话的意思是，听着，唐纳德·特朗普认为华尔街建设了美国。

sentences.en: Ordinary middle-class Americans built America.
sentences.zh: 是普通的美国中产阶级建设了美国。

sentences.en: My dad used to have an expression.
sentences.zh: 我爸爸过去常说一句话。

sentences.en: He said, Joe, a job is about a lot more than a paycheck.
sentences.zh: 他说，乔，工作不仅仅是一张薪水支票那么简单。

sentences.en: He doesn't repudiate his remarks.
sentences.zh: 他并没有否认自己先前的言论。

sentences.en: He doesn't go back on them and say, actually, I will go after the wealthy.
sentences.zh: 他没有收回那些话并说“其实我会对富人采取行动”。

sentences.en: And the contrast with Sanders, he really leaves implicit that his focus is going to be on providing new benefits to the middle class.
sentences.zh: 他和桑德斯的对比，实际上不言而喻地表明他的重点将放在为中产阶级提供新的福利上。

sentences.en: They have to have insurance that is covered and they can afford it.
sentences.zh: 他们必须拥有能够得到保障且负担得起的保险。

sentences.en: They have to make sure that we're in a situation where there's continuing education and they're able to pay for it.
sentences.zh: 他们必须确保我们处于一种能够获得持续教育并且支付得起学费的环境中。

sentences.en: These are pretty conventional liberal policies.
sentences.zh: 这些都是相当传统的自由主义政策。

sentences.en: They are not blow-it-up policies.
sentences.zh: 它们并不是什么彻底推翻重来的政策。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So in these first two exchanges, we right away have this division that we have been talking about with you.
sentences.zh: 因此，在头两轮交锋中，我们立刻就看到了我们一直与你讨论过的那种分歧。

sentences.en: These two leading candidates on either poll, restoration versus sweeping change.
sentences.zh: 民调领先的这两位候选人，代表着恢复现状与彻底变革的对立。

sentences.en: And it really intensifies exactly along those lines for the first couple stages of the debate.
sentences.zh: 在辩论的前几个阶段，这种对比完全沿着这些路线急剧加剧。

sentences.en: And unlike on Wednesday night, you had some real fire on the more moderate side.
sentences.zh: 与周三晚上不同，温和派阵营这次出现了一些真正的火药味。

sentences.en: The bottom line is, if we don't clearly define that we are not socialists, the Republicans are going to come at us every way they can and call us socialists.
sentences.zh: 最底线的是，如果我们不明确划清界限表明我们不是社会主义者，共和党人就会想方设法攻击我们，把我们叫作社会主义者。

sentences.en: You had folks like John Hickenlooper, the Colorado governor, come right out at the top, directly taking on Bernie Sanders.
sentences.zh: 像科罗拉多州州长约翰·希肯卢珀这样的人，一上来就直接针锋相对地挑战了伯尼·桑德斯。

sentences.en: When Senator Sanders says that Canada is single-payer, there are 35 million people in Canada.
sentences.zh: 当桑德斯参议员说加拿大是单一支付方医疗体制时，加拿大有3500万人口。

sentences.en: There are 330 million people in the United States, easily the number of people on a public option.
sentences.zh: 而美国有3.3亿人口，这完全相当于公共选择方案的人数规模。

sentences.en: You had Michael Bennett a little later in the debate come out and really, really stress this
sentences.zh: 稍后在辩论中，迈克尔·贝内特站出来，非常、非常强调了

sentences.en: one element of the Bernie Sanders health care plan that many Democrats and a lot of Republicans see as politically toxic.
sentences.zh: 伯尼·桑德斯医疗计划中的这一要素，许多民主党人和许多共和党人都认为这在政治上是有毒的。

sentences.en: He has said over and over again, unlike others that have supported this legislation, over and
sentences.zh: 他一再表示，与支持这项立法的其他人不同，他一次又一次地强调

sentences.en: over again, that this will ban, make illegal all insurance except cosmetic, except insurance for, I guess that's for plastic surgery.
sentences.zh: 这将取缔、将所有保险宣布为非法，除了美容整形保险，我想那是针对整容手术的。

sentences.en: That is a much, much more forceful counterpunch against the more left-wing, comprehensive reform type candidates than we heard from anyone on Wednesday.
sentences.zh: 相比我们在周三听到的任何人，这是对偏左翼、全盘改革型候选人更有力、更有力的反击。

sentences.en: So finally, there's some actual fighting over these two approaches.
sentences.zh: 所以总算有人针对这两种方法展开了真正的争论。

sentences.en: And some real fighting on behalf of the more moderate wing of the party that, you know, on
sentences.zh: 为了该党的温和派翼翼，也展开了一些真正的战斗，你知道的，在周三

sentences.en: Wednesday we heard Elizabeth Warren make her argument for big structural change with, at best, a kind of passive-aggressive pushback on that.
sentences.zh: 我们听到伊丽莎白·沃伦为宏大的结构性变革做出了辩护，而受到的反弹充其量也只是一种被动攻击型的回击。

sentences.en: We got just aggressive-aggressive pushback tonight.
sentences.zh: 而今晚我们遇到的是彻头彻尾的主动攻击型回击。

sentences.en: Well, how did these candidates differentiate themselves when it came to the specifics of the policies that they advocate for?
sentences.zh: 那么，当涉及到他们所倡导的政策细节时，这些候选人是如何区分彼此的？

sentences.en: Well, much as we saw on Wednesday night, health care was a really, really crucial differentiator.
sentences.zh: 嗯，正如我们在周三晚上所看到的，医疗保健是一个非常、非常关键的分水岭。

sentences.en: We asked a question about health care last night that spurred a lot of discussion, as you know.
sentences.zh: 正如你所知，我们昨晚提出的关于医疗保健的问题引发了许多讨论。

sentences.en: We're going to do it again now.
sentences.zh: 我们现在要再来一次。

sentences.en: There was another, you know, raise your hand if you support displacing the private health insurance system question.
sentences.zh: 还有一个问题，你知道的，支持取消私人医疗保险系统的人请举手。

sentences.en: There were not a lot of takers for that one that you saw.
sentences.zh: 正如你所见，当时应和的人并不多。

sentences.en: Bernie Sanders, you saw Kamala Harris go in for that.
sentences.zh: 伯尼·桑德斯，你看到卡玛拉·哈里斯也加入了这一阵营。

sentences.en: I think it does show you between the two nights that that does remain a real lefty litmus test that even some pretty progressive candidates are not entirely comfortable embracing.
sentences.zh: 我认为这确实向你表明，在这两晚之间，这仍然是一个真正的左翼试金石，甚至一些相当激进的候选人也并非完全乐意接受它。

sentences.en: I thought it was especially striking that Harris raised her hand for that.
sentences.zh: 我认为哈里斯为这一点举手尤其引人注目。

sentences.en: On Thursday, the Supreme Court issued two rulings about how power and resources are allocated.
sentences.zh: 周四，最高法院就权力与资源的分配问题发布了两项裁决。

sentences.en: In the first case, the court ruled that federal courts have no authority to challenge partisan
sentences.zh: 在第一起案件中，法院裁定联邦法院无权对党派

sentences.en: gerrymandering, finding that that power resides with the state lawmakers who draw election districts.
sentences.zh: 划定选区（gerrymandering）提出异议，并认为这一权力属于绘制选举选区的州议员。

sentences.en: The decision will reinforce the tactic of creating voting districts that deliberately favor a single party.
sentences.zh: 这一裁决将巩固故意偏袒单一政党的划定选区策略。

sentences.en: In the second case, the court found that the Trump administration has not offered a compelling justification for adding a question about citizenship to the 2020 census.
sentences.zh: 在第二起案件中，法院裁定特朗普政府未能提供令人信服的理由，以在2020年人口普查中增加关于国籍的问题。

sentences.en: The justices found that the administration had relied on a contrived explanation for asking about citizenship on the census.
sentences.zh: 大法官们发现，政府在普查中询问国籍的问题时依赖于一个牵强的解释。

sentences.en: For now, the ruling will prevent a census question that critics feared would discourage undocumented
sentences.zh: 目前，这项裁决将阻止一个普查问题，批评者曾担心该问题会阻止无证
